correctness.rationale: For each \(n\), \(c\le\min(r,n-r+1)\le\lceil n/2\rceil\). Every fixed domain/image pair admits at most \(2^c c!\) induced-path isomorphisms and there are \(4^n\) ordered pairs. One fixed independent set of k vertices gives k! distinct maps for every \(0\le k\le h\). These yield both finite factorial probability sandwiches and Stirling gives exact scaled logarithmic rates. Inequalities \(c\le n-r+1\) and \(2c+e\le n+1\) give the high rank and induced-edge tails. An independent brute-force map enumerator agrees with run-type enumeration for all \(n\le6\); all \(n\le20\) tested cases satisfy the finite bounds. The infinite theorem follows from the proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The component count stratifies induced-subgraph isomorphism types of an inverse monoid, and domain cardinality is its canonical rank. This identifies dominant large-path local symmetries and gives sharp rare-event probabilities for every fixed linear deficit, rather than merely a finite counting exercise or a previously known overall cardinality. It explains concentration on almost-independent supports, a structural asymptotic law for a natural infinite family.
